response:
I'm sorry you're carrying that weight — what your ex made you feel says more about them than about you. Rebuilding self-esteem starts with noticing when those old critical voices show up and gently challenging them with evidence of your actual worth. Try writing down moments you felt proud of yourself, even small ones, to build a more accurate picture of who you are.

When overthinking pulls you back to the past, grounding techniques can help — try naming things you see, hear, and feel right now to bring yourself into the present. Consider setting a "worry window," a limited time to process those thoughts, then redirecting your focus afterward. Surrounding yourself with people who genuinely value you matters too, as their perspective can slowly replace the distorted one your ex imposed. If these patterns feel deeply stuck, a counselor can help you unpack them in a safe space. You deserve to see yourself clearly, and healing is absolutely possible — one small step at a time.
